title: Three Scales Thermometer
creator: Hank R. & Claude Code
subject: Environmental Monitoring
description: Fahrenheit, Celsius and kelvin on one shared physical column, with a difference mode that shows why 5 degrees of warming is 9 Fahrenheit degrees and not 41.

learningObjectives: Convert a temperature between Fahrenheit, Celsius and kelvin.
Distinguish converting a temperature value from converting a temperature difference.

keyQuestions: Why do Celsius and kelvin give the same number for a difference?
The forecast says it will warm by 10 C tonight. How many Fahrenheit degrees is that?
What is special about 0 K that is not special about 0 C?
commonMisconceptions: Applying the +32 offset to a temperature change.
Believing 98.6 F is a precise measurement rather than a conversion of 37 C.
Thinking kelvin is just Celsius with a different name.
assessmentOpportunities: Converts in both directions between all three scales.
Explains why kelvin and Celsius differences are numerically identical.
States that a temperature difference does not take the +32 offset.
